brief: The gardener is the rarest person in the garden the town is named for. `LAWN_W = {gardener: 0.15, ...}` is a SHARE of a single roll and the gardener's sub-cap is 1, so #121's `LAWN_CAP` 4 -> 8 moved every lawn kind except this one: gardener presence went 0.65 -> 0.63. #121 also established that the SUB-CAPS, not the cap, are the limiter now — twelve places, of which only seven exist below `LAWN_LIE_WARMTH` — so the lever here is the gardener's own supply, not the lawn's. Give the gardener a schedule instead of a lottery ticket: someone works the beds on most growing-season mornings, at an hour that reads. The work itself is already legible (`gardenerKneel`, `GARDEN_REACH`, `a.rowDur` work a row at a time) and the beds already know their own state through `growF`/`dieF`/`bloomCap`. Closes c185 and c186 together.
successLooksLike: Measured with probes/lawn-day.mjs over a full year, gardener presence on a growing-season morning is at least 3x HEAD's and does not fall away when the lawn is busy; midwinter and wet days are unchanged.
avoid: Do not raise LAWN_CAP — #121 swept it 2..12 and 8 is the knee. A share of a roll is not a rate: if the gardener needs its own source, give it one and follow spawnLawnAgent's pattern rather than reweighting LAWN_W and hoping. And raising one kind inside a fixed set of place-holders takes places from another — sweep it and report WHICH kind absorbed the change, because that composition shift is nobody's brief.
